memory_update.text: LINC and UTI are the cleanest direct-capacity public mappings for employer-aligned skilled-trades training; both should be tracked for student starts, placement, employer partnerships, and campus/program expansion.

SNA is a hidden supplier candidate because its certification, student tool, diagnostics, curriculum, and NC3-linked technical-education programs may benefit from vocational lab expansion, but revenue materiality needs verification.

LECO is a hidden supplier candidate for welding-program capacity through machines, consumables, virtual welding simulators, robotic cells, and curriculum/training-center assets, but education-specific revenue is not yet proven.

Need a follow-up search for micro/small public suppliers of HVAC lab equipment, healthcare simulation labs, industrial-maintenance trainers, credentialing software, campus real estate, and exam/proctoring services tied to vocational schools.

summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around the scarce-capacity node of employer-aligned skilled-trades training. The most direct public-market mappings are small-cap vocational operators with campuses, instructors, labs, employer partnerships, and regulated program capacity. The underfollowed supplier lane includes industrial tool, certification, welding, simulator, and curriculum/equipment vendors whose education exposure is usually hidden inside broader industrial segments rather than screened as education companies.
